script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: BLOOM

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

We open on a sunlit suburban neighborhood. The camera pans down a street, where children play in front yards and neighbors chat with each other.

NARRATOR (V.O.) (Female)
(whispering)
In this quiet little suburban neighborhood, where everyone knows each other, secrets lie just beneath the surface.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

We enter the living room of the SMITH FAMILY. MRS. SMITH (40s) and MR. SMITH (50s) sit on the couch, their son MAX (12) sits on the floor, engrossed in a comic book.

MRS. SMITH
Max, dear, can you please set the table for dinner?

MAX
(looking up from comic book)
Sure, Mom.

As he gets up, MR. SMITH'S phone rings. He answers it.

MR. SMITH
Yes, this is Bob Smith.

CUT TO:

EXT. SCHOOL YARD - DAY

We see PRINCIPAL WILLIAMS (50s) pacing nervously. MR. SMITH arrives, looking worried.

PRINCIPAL WILLIAMS
Mr. Smith, I have some concerning news. Max has been acting out in school. Drawing disturbing pictures, causing disruptions in class.

MR. SMITH
(shocked)
What?! Max has always been such a good student.

PRINCIPAL WILLIAMS
I understand, but we need to get to the bottom of this. I'd like to arrange a meeting with you, Max, and the school counselor.

CUT TO:

INT. SMITH KITCHEN - NIGHT

MR. SMITH sits at the table, looking at Max's troubling artwork. Max enters the kitchen, looking apologetic.

MAX
Dad, I'm sorry about the pictures. I didn't mean to upset anyone.

MR. SMITH
(sighs)
Max, we need to talk about what's been going on at school. Why have you been drawing these pictures?

MAX
I don't know. I just feel...different, I guess. Like I don't belong here.

CUT TO:

INT. SCHOOL COUNSELOR'S OFFICE - DAY

The Smith family sits in the office of COUNSELOR JENKINS (30s).

COUNSELOR JENKINS
Max, I'd like to understand a little more about what you've been feeling lately. Can you tell me about any changes in your life that might be causing these feelings?

MAX
(hesitant)
I don't know. I guess nothing really big has happened. I just feel like I don't fit in.

COUNSELOR JENKINS
(nods)
It's natural to feel that way sometimes, Max. But it's important to remember that everyone is unique, and there's no one "right" way to be. Have you considered talking to anyone about these feelings? Maybe a friend or a family member?

MAX
(sighs)
I have, but they don't seem to understand. They all just want me to be like everyone else.

CUT TO:

EXT. PARK - DAY

Max sits on a bench in the park, drawing in his sketchbook. A STREET ARTIST (20s) approaches, noticing Max's artwork.

STREET ARTIST
Hey there, little artist. I see you've got some talent.

MAX
(shyly)
Thank you.

STREET ARTIST
You know, sometimes it's hard to be different. But difference is what makes the world interesting. Have you ever thought about sharing your art with the world?

MAX
(excited)
Really? You think someone would want to see my art?

STREET ARTIST
Absolutely. Talent like yours doesn't go unnoticed.

CUT TO:

INT. SMITH KITCHEN - NIGHT

Max shows his parents his artwork, which has been accepted into a local art show. They are proud of him, and Max finally feels like he belongs.

NARRATOR (V.O.) (Female)
In a world where everyone tries to fit in, it's the differences that make us unique. And sometimes, all it takes is a little encouragement to bloom.

FADE OUT.
